claim.pdf_says: Page 1024 (printed 994) ends with "Modi:\n11630-11640, 11650-11659". "Mongolian:" is the FIRST line printed on page 1025 (printed 995), directly above "180B-180D, 1810-1819, 18A9".
claim.markdown_says: End of the page-1024 block: "Modi:\n11630-11640, 11650-11659 Mongolian:". The page-1025 block then opens with a headless "180B-180D, 1810-1819, 18A9".
claim.why_it_matters: Mongolian's code-point ranges are left unattributed in the normative Annex B table and the Modi entry carries a stray label.

verdict.reasoning:
The claim's description of both sources is factually accurate, but the difference it describes is pure page-break furniture and changes no content and no meaning. Refuted on four independent grounds.

(1) VERIFIED THE SOURCES. Rendered spec_p1024.png at 300dpi: the last two content lines printed on page 1024 (folio 994) are 'Modi:' then '11630-11640, 11650-11659', followed by whitespace, the folio '994  (C)ISO/IEC 2023' and the license footer. No 'Mongolian:' appears anywhere on page 1024. Rendered spec_p1025.png: its first content line is indeed 'Mongolian:', directly above '180B-180D, 1810-1819, 18A9'. Markdown specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 40928 (last line of the page-1024 block) reads '11630-11640, 11650-11659 Mongolian:', and the page-1025 block opens at line 40936 with '180B-180D, 1810-1819, 18A9'. So both quotations check out.

(2) NOTHING IS MISSING; READING ORDER IS EXACTLY PRESERVED. 'Mongolian:' is present in the markdown, and it is on the line immediately adjacent to its own data, separated only by the injected page-boundary furniture ('', '## Page 1025', '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)'). Strip that furniture -- which is transcription scaffolding, not spec text -- and the stream reads '... Modi: / 11630-11640, 11650-11659 / Mongolian: / 180B-180D, 1810-1819, 18A9', i.e. exactly the PDF's reading order with exactly the PDF's attribution. This falls squarely under the refutation criterion 'the missing text is actually present (possibly reflowed or on an adjacent line)'.

(3) THE 'WHY IT MATTERS' IS OVERSTATED ON BOTH COUNTS. 'Mongolian's ranges are left unattributed' is false -- the label 'Mongolian:' directly precedes '180B-180D, 1810-1819, 18A9' in the text stream; no reader or parser following the flow loses the association. 'The Modi entry carries a stray label' overstates it too: Modi's ranges are transcribed complete and correct ('11630-11640, 11650-11659'), and the trailing token is unambiguously the next entry's heading -- a capitalized script name terminated by a colon, the exact shape of every other label in the table. Modi's data is not corrupted or ambiguated.

(4) IT IS A GLOBAL PIPELINE PAGE-SPLIT BEHAVIOR, NOT A PAGE-1024 CONTENT DEFECT. The transcription's page boundary is placed one line late at every page break in these Unicode script listings. A regex for 'hex-ranges<space>Label:' finds ~19 instances across the two script tables: lines 40182 (Ahom), 40235 (Buhid), 40403 (Kaithi), 40454 (Linear_B), 40506 (Miao), 40558 (Old_Italic), 40610 (Rejang), 40772 (Buhid), 40824 (Gunjala_Gondi), 40876 (Khojki), 40928 (Mongolian -- this claim), 40981 (Sharada), 49030 (Brahmi), 49087 (Deseret), 49207 (Kannada), 49263 (Lydian), 49319 (Multani), 49374 (Old_Turkic), 49431 (Sinhala). The same defect is present at the TOP of page 1024 itself and the claim does not mention it: the PDF's first page-1024 line 'Khojki:' was pulled up to line 40876, so the page-1024 block also opens headless with '1122C-11237, 1123E'. Singling out the bottom edge while ignoring the identical top edge shows the claim is describing a boundary convention, not lost content.

(5) THE REST OF PAGE 1024 IS A CLEAN MATCH. I compared all 16 script entries on the rendered page against the markdown block line by line -- Khojki, Khudawadi, Lao, Lepcha, Limbu, Mahajani, Makasar, Malayalam (both wrapped lines), Mandaic, Manichaean, Marchen, Masaram_Gondi, Meetei_Mayek, Mende_Kikakui, Miao, Modi. Every label and every code-point range is transcribed identically. There is no content discrepancy on this page.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The transcription splits pages one line late throughout the Annex Unicode script tables, so each page block ends with the next page's first label appended to its own last data line and the next block opens headless. Here 'Mongolian:' sits at the end of the page-1024 block instead of the start of the page-1025 block -- and symmetrically 'Khojki:', the PDF's first page-1024 line, sits at the end of the page-1023 block. No text is lost, no label is detached from its ranges in reading order, and every one of page 1024's 16 script entries matches the PDF exactly. If anything is to be ledgered it is a single global note about page-boundary placement in the extraction pipeline (~19 occurrences, listed in the reasoning), at cosmetic severity -- not a structural, per-page finding.
